# Phase 9 — the `*mut sWelsEncCtx` fork-split census (S63)

*Generated by `python3 rust/tools/phase9_forksplit.py --list` at Phase 9 session
E3's close (commit `3a1d39b7`). **Re-run it before quoting** — that is the whole
point of it being a tool (S24). This document is the snapshot G's brief is
scoped from; the tool is the authority.*

## The number G's brief must carry

| | bodies |
|---|---:|
| **in-fork** — end state is interior mutability (the seam's shape) or lawful raw | **111** |
| **ST-flippable** — a root-down campaign can convert these | **157** |
| total bodies with a `*mut sWelsEncCtx` parameter | **268** |

Reconciliation with the grep the charter quotes: `grep -rn ': \*mut sWelsEncCtx'
src/encoder | grep -v ':\s*//' | wc -l` reads **285** *mentions* at this commit
(287 at the E3 brief's commit, less `ctx_pic_ref_mut` and
`StampLayerPictureViews`, both deleted this session). 285 mentions = 268 function
bodies + 13 mentions inside `pub type` fn-pointer typedefs + 4 second-parameter
and `*mut *mut` spellings. **The unit is the body**, because fork-reachability is
a property of a body, not of a token (S24's unit clause).

## What the split means

S63, from F146: the in-fork half **cannot take `&mut` by any amount of hazard
work**. The blocker is not a held cursor but N workers performing concurrent
entry retags of one allocation, so a clean `q1c.py` reading on such a body is
necessary and irrelevant. Its two lawful end states are interior mutability
(`rec_view.rs`'s shape, D-mt-3) or permanent tagged raw. The ST column is the
half G can flip J-model root-down.

## Method, and its one interesting arm

Seeds are the three `std::thread::scope` spawn closures in
`slice_multi_threading.rs`; the walk closes transitively over named calls,
`pf*` dispatch slots (every installee of a slot an in-fork body calls through),
and **arrays of function items**. That third arm is the one that decides the
answer: `WelsCodeOneSlice` reaches all four mode-decision drivers through the
static table `g_pWelsSliceCoding`, not through a `pf` slot, so a walker that
knows only named calls and slots reports the **entire MD surface as
single-threaded**. Calibrated by knocking the dispatch arms out (`--no-slots`):
**27 in-fork with them off, 111 with them on** — the arms are 84 bodies, and a
tool that had never been shown to move would not be evidence (S55/S58).

Spot-checks (`--why`):

```
WelsMdInterMb <- WelsMdInterMbLoop <- WelsPSliceMdEnc <- WelsCodePSlice
              <- WelsCodePSlice_c <- WelsCodeOneSlice
              <- EncodeOnePartitionSizeLimited <- fork seed
WelsRcMbInit  <- WelsISliceMdEncDynamic <- WelsISliceMdEncDynamic_c
              <- WelsCodeOneSlice <- EncodeOneSliceInJob <- fork seed
WelsInitEncoderExt is NOT fork-reachable
```

It is an **over-approximation on purpose** (the plane census's trade): a body
reached only under a configuration the fork never takes still lands in the
in-fork column, because a false negative there is a data race with no gate
behind it. Two known over-counts: a slot's *other* installee (only one
`pfInterMd` runs per layer; both are pulled in), and helpers shared between a
fork path and an init path.
